# A stage's transform is handed the resolved result as JSON on stdin and its stdout
# becomes the stage's summary — the short answer to "and what does that mean?",
# next to (never instead of) the raw output. It can be any command: jq as plain
# argv, an inline python or sh script, or a binary of your own.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

exec breeze register identity ci
cp stdout ci.token
exec breeze apply -f pipeline.hcl --as ci --token-file ci.token

# An inline sh transform, on a stage that failed. The summary explains; the exit
# status is still the stage's own.
! exec breeze start stage svc failing abc123 --as ci --token-file ci.token
stdout 'failing: failed'
stdout '2 of 3 checks failed'

# The raw output is kept — a summary never replaces the record. (status exits
# non-zero because the STAGE failed, which is the documented convention.)
! exec breeze status stage svc failing abc123 --json
stdout '"stdout":\s*"[^"]*not ok'
stdout '"summary":\s*"2 of 3 checks failed"'

# A bare command name is looked up on PATH, not anchored at the config file: this
# is what `command = ["jq", ...]` in a transform depends on.
exec breeze start stage svc pathlookup abc123 --as ci --token-file ci.token
stdout 'pathlookup: succeeded'
stdout 'echo found on PATH'

# A transform that breaks cannot turn a green stage red, and does not vanish either.
exec breeze start stage svc broken abc123 --as ci --token-file ci.token
stdout 'broken: succeeded'
stdout 'transform exited 7'

# A stage with no transform is unaffected and carries no summary.
exec breeze start stage svc plain abc123 --as ci --token-file ci.token
stdout 'plain: succeeded'
exec breeze status stage svc plain abc123 --json
! stdout '"summary"'

exec breeze stop

-- pipeline.hcl --
pipeline "svc" {
  stage "failing" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "20s"
    command = ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo 'ok 1'; echo 'not ok 2'; echo 'not ok 3'; exit 1"]
    transform {
      timeout = "20s"
      script  = <<-SH
        json=$(cat)
        total=$(printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o 'ok ' | wc -l)
        bad=$(printf '%s' "$json" | grep -o 'not ok' | wc -l)
        echo "$bad of $total checks failed"
      SH
    }
  }

  stage "pathlookup" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "20s"
    command = ["/bin/true"]
    transform {
      command = ["echo", "echo found on PATH"]
      timeout = "20s"
    }
  }

  stage "broken" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "20s"
    command = ["/bin/true"]
    transform {
      timeout = "20s"
      script  = "exit 7"
    }
  }

  stage "plain" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "20s"
    command = ["/bin/true"]
  }
}
